chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Al-Husayn ibn Atiyya, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him), said:

He was seated in the Masjid, and I was with him, so he heard the voice of a man being whipped at the morning prayer on a day of intense cold. He said: 'What is this?' They said, 'A man being whipped.' He said: 'Glory be to Allah! In a time like this? No one is whipped regarding any of the fixed penalties during winter except during the last hour of the day, nor in summer except during the coldest part of the day.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rulings on the timing of corporal punishment (hudud) during extreme weather conditions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the jurisprudential principle of 'raf' al-haraj' (removal of hardship) by linking the physical severity of the punishment to environmental conditions. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the humane application of hudud, ensuring that the penalty does not become disproportionately cruel due to extreme heat or cold, thereby preserving the dignity of the offender.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, from Al Husayn Bin Atiyya, from Hisham Bin Ahmad, from Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was seated in the Masjid, and I was with him, so he<sup>asws</sup> heard the voice of a man being whipped, at the morning Prayer on a day of intense cold. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is this?’ So they said, ‘A man being whipped’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! During a time like this? They should not whip anyone with regards to anything from the Penalties during the winter except during the last hour of the day, nor in the summer except during the coldest time of what happens from the day’.
